title: Who Is the Sell-By Date Really For?

fin.big: Simplified illustrations. Not food safety advice.
fin.small: Sources: UK government (Defra), press release, 15 Sep 2011; Food Standards Agency; Marks & Spencer history (company account, via MyLearning)

parts: Sell by. Display until. Those dates are not really written for you.
In twenty eleven, the British government said it in plain words.
Sell-by and display-until labels are used for stock rotation.
In other words, they help the shop sell the older packs first.
And the government asked for them to be removed, to avoid shopper confusion.
So which dates are meant for you?
Use by, for food that could become unsafe after that date.
And best before, which is about quality.
But Marks and Spencer first used date codes in nineteen seventy, one account says, several years before they were compulsory.
Our reading: the date started as a tool for the shop, and only later became a tool for you.
So why does one tin carry a code no shopper can read? The full story is in the video linked below.
